title: Set up the shared mailbox PIM Manager sends mail from
purpose: Set up the shared mailbox PIM Manager sends its notification mail from: create the mailbox, give each sending identity a send right scoped to that one mailbox (Exchange RBAC for applications), remove any tenant-wide Microsoft Graph Mail.Send from those identities, and store the sender in the PIM store.
whenToRun: Once per environment, when PIM Manager > Get Started > Mail sender (shared mailbox) or the end-of-install check says the mail sender is not set up -- typically because the install ran as a person without an Exchange role. Run it again at any time: every step reads first and an environment that is already set up is left unchanged. Needs an Exchange Online plan in the tenant (EXCHANGE_S_FOUNDATION alone is not enough).

runAs.name: Exchange Administrator (or Global Administrator)
runAs.scope: the tenant (an ACTIVE assignment -- activate it first if it is eligible)
runAs.why: Browser sign-in (the default): the person's own Exchange role creates the mailbox, the Exchange registrations, the management scope and the scoped Application Mail.Send assignments. No app is granted any Exchange right in this mode.

runAs.name: Delegated Microsoft Graph consent: Organization.Read.All, Application.Read.All, User.Read.All, AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All (public client Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools)
runAs.why: Reads the Exchange plan (subscribedSkus), the initial domain (organization), the sending identities' service principals and the mailbox's directory user; AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All is used only to remove a tenant-wide Mail.Send. The consent prompt appears at the first sign-in when the tenant has not consented yet.

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator or Global Administrator
runAs.why: Only when a sending identity or the engine identity still holds a tenant-wide Microsoft Graph Mail.Send: removing an application permission needs one of these roles besides the delegated AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All. An Exchange Administrator alone can do every other step.

runAs.name: Reader
runAs.scope: the Container Apps job and/or Manager container app named by -TickJobName / -ManagerAppName (or their resource group)
runAs.why: Only with -SubscriptionId -ResourceGroup -TickJobName / -ManagerAppName: reads the app's managed identity so its object id does not have to be typed.

runAs.name: Member of the environment's SQL admin group (grp-pim-sql-admins)
runAs.why: Only with -SqlServerFqdn: stores MailSender and MailMode. From a computer that cannot reach the store this step is reported as 'Saved: no ... Finish in PIM Manager' (Get Started > Mail sender > Check and send a test mail) and is not a failure in the browser sign-in -- or, with -AllowThisIpTemporarily, a temporary firewall rule is added (see below).

runAs.name: SQL Server Contributor (or Contributor)
runAs.why: Only with -AllowThisIpTemporarily: adds a temporary firewall rule for the refused IP and removes it again in the same run.

runAs.name: Invardia Support app (-AdminAppId + -AdminSecret) holding Microsoft Graph application permissions AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All and RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory
runAs.why: Only for the unattended support / deploy path instead of a person: the app gives ITSELF Exchange.ManageAsApp and activates a time-bound Exchange Administrator through PIM (see changes). When the app cannot grant itself, the signed-in az session of a Global Administrator is used for those two grants only.

changes.object: shared mailbox <MailboxName>@<initial domain> (New-Mailbox -Shared; default PIM-Engine@<tenant>.onmicrosoft.com, display name 'PIM Manager (notifications)')
changes.why: The address PIM Manager sends its notifications from. A shared mailbox needs no licence and no password; nobody signs in to it.
changes.undo: Remove the mailbox (Exchange admin center > Mailboxes, or Remove-Mailbox) -- PIM Manager then stops sending mail.

changes.object: Exchange registration of each sending identity (New-ServicePrincipal with the identity's app id and object id): the engine job's and the Manager's managed identity, or the engine application when no managed identity sends
changes.why: Exchange RBAC for applications can only assign a role to a service principal Exchange knows.
changes.undo: Remove-ServicePrincipal -Identity <app id> (after removing its role assignment).

changes.object: management scope -ScopeName (default <MailboxName>-SendScope; a scope that already restricts to this mailbox -- e.g. PIM4EntraPS-Sender from an earlier release -- is kept under its own name, never duplicated) with RecipientRestrictionFilter PrimarySmtpAddress -eq '<sender>' (New-ManagementScope)
changes.scope: exactly one recipient: the sender mailbox
changes.why: Limits the send right below to this one mailbox. A scope that already exists for ANOTHER mailbox is never reused or changed (the run stops instead).
changes.undo: Remove-ManagementScope -Identity <scope name> (after removing the assignments that use it).

changes.object: each sending identity (New-ManagementRoleAssignment, name <AssignmentNamePrefix>-<short id>-MailSend or <AssignmentNamePrefix>-App-MailSend; an assignment the identity already holds -- e.g. PIM4EntraPS-MI-<id>-MailSend -- is kept, never duplicated)
changes.permission: Exchange role 'Application Mail.Send' (Exchange RBAC for applications)
changes.scope: the management scope above = the sender mailbox only
changes.why: Lets PIM Manager's engine and Manager send as that one mailbox and no other. This is the ONLY send right the script grants -- there is no tenant-wide Mail.Send.

changes.object: a sending identity's Application Mail.Send assignment on ANOTHER sender scope of PIM Manager (<mailbox>-SendScope or PIM4EntraPS-Sender*; Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment) -- and, only with -RemoveEngineSpnAssignment, the engine application's older assignment on this scope
changes.why: An identity scoped to another environment's mailbox would send as the wrong mailbox (assignment names are tenant-unique, so the right one cannot be created beside it). The engine application's own older assignment is left in place unless explicitly asked.
changes.undo: Re-create it with New-ManagementRoleAssignment (same name, role, app and scope).

changes.object: the organization: Enable-OrganizationCustomization -- only when the organization is still 'dehydrated'
changes.why: A new Exchange organization refuses every custom RBAC object until customization is enabled.
changes.undo: None -- Microsoft offers no way back, and it changes nothing visible.

changes.object: application permission (app role assignment) Microsoft Graph Mail.Send held TENANT-WIDE by a sending identity or the engine identity
changes.scope: the tenant (the assignment being removed was tenant-wide)
changes.why: A tenant-wide Mail.Send lets the identity send as ANY mailbox and silently defeats the per-mailbox scope above (measured: with it, an out-of-scope send is accepted). Removing it makes the scope govern.
changes.undo: Not recommended. Re-grant Mail.Send (application) to that identity in Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > the identity > Permissions.

changes.object: pim.Settings rows MailSender (the mailbox's directory UPN -- the key Microsoft Graph sends as) and MailMode = sharedMailbox, plus MailSenderSetupCheck (the read-back that confirmed the scoped Mail.Send for every sending identity in one scope, so PIM Manager shows the engine job's send right as granted once its own test mail works)
changes.why: Only with -SqlServerFqdn. The engine and the Manager read the sender from here; without it the mail is rendered and never sent.
changes.undo: PIM Manager > Settings > Mail & alerting: choose another sender or mode.

changes.object: a TEMPORARY firewall rule PimSetupTemp-<ip>-<utc time> for exactly the refused IP -- only with -AllowThisIpTemporarily and only when the store refused this computer
changes.scope: the environment's SQL server, one IP
changes.why: Lets this computer store the sender when the SQL firewall refuses it. Removed again in the same run (finally), whether the write worked or not; a rule that could not be removed is reported with its name.
changes.undo: It is removed by the run. If the run reports it could not: SQL server > Networking > remove the PimSetupTemp-* rule.

changes.target: Microsoft Graph (Invardia Support app sign-in only)
changes.permission: Exchange.ManageAsApp (application permission of Office 365 Exchange Online)
changes.why: App-only Exchange administration needs it. Not used and not granted in the browser sign-in. It has no expiry but is inert without the directory role below.
changes.undo: Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > the setup app > Permissions: remove Exchange.ManageAsApp.

changes.target: Microsoft Entra ID (Invardia Support app sign-in only)
changes.object: the setup app itself (-AdminAppId), through PIM (roleAssignmentScheduleRequests, time-bound)
changes.permission: Exchange Administrator directory role (active, -ExchangeAdminDuration, default PT4H)
changes.why: Exchange accepts the app's admin calls only while it holds an Exchange role. Granted through PIM so it EXPIRES by itself; an assignment that is already active is reused, and one that lasts longer than asked is reported as standing privilege.
changes.undo: It expires by itself. To end it sooner: Entra admin center > Roles > Exchange Administrator > Active assignments > remove (a different administrator: an identity cannot remove its own role).

changes.target: Microsoft Graph (Invardia Support app sign-in only)
changes.object: the setup app itself (-AdminAppId) -- self-heal, only when it does not hold it yet
changes.why: Needed to read and request the time-bound Exchange Administrator role above. A setup identity created before 2026-09-26 lacks it; it holds AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All, which is exactly the right to add it.
changes.undo: Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > the setup app > Permissions: remove RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory.

changes.object: the result file named by -OutFile (JSON: ok, sender, steps, privileged grants); a transcript in <temp>\pim-manager-logs
changes.why: -OutFile: how a deploy step reads the outcome. The transcript is the local record of what the run did (no secret values).

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant id. A sign-in that lands in another tenant is refused.

parameters.name: ManagedIdentityObjectId
parameters.help: Object ids of the managed identities that send (the engine job's and the Manager's), comma-separated. PIM Manager's Get Started fills them in. A service principal that is not a managed identity is refused.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: With -ResourceGroup and -TickJobName / -ManagerAppName: read those apps' managed identities from Azure instead of typing their ids (added to -ManagedIdentityObjectId).

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: Resource group of the engine job / Manager app (see -SubscriptionId).

parameters.name: TickJobName
parameters.help: The engine's Container Apps job (e.g. ca-pim-tick); its managed identity is resolved by the same rule the engine uses.

parameters.name: ManagerAppName
parameters.help: The Manager's container app (e.g. ca-pim-manager); it sends the alert notices.

parameters.name: SqlServerFqdn
parameters.help: The environment's SQL server (<server>.database.windows.net). With it the sender is stored in pim.Settings; without it the script tells you to finish in PIM Manager.

parameters.name: SqlDatabase
parameters.help: The store database.

parameters.name: MailboxName
parameters.help: Your organisation's name for the sender mailbox (the part before the @). PIM Manager > Get Started > Mail sender step 1 fills it in. A mailbox that already exists at that address is used as it is.

parameters.name: MailDomain
parameters.help: Domain of the sender mailbox. Never guessed: a domain that does not receive mail gives a mailbox nobody can reply to.

parameters.name: DisplayName
parameters.help: Display name of the mailbox (what recipients see as the sender).

parameters.name: ScopeName
parameters.help: Name of the Exchange management scope. A scope that already restricts to this mailbox is kept under its own name.

parameters.name: AssignmentNamePrefix
parameters.help: Prefix of the Exchange role-assignment names (<prefix>-<short id>-MailSend). Assignments the sending identities already hold are kept under their own names.

parameters.name: AllowThisIpTemporarily
parameters.help: Opt-in: when the PIM database refuses this computer (Azure SQL firewall), add a temporary firewall rule for exactly the refused IP, store the sender, and always remove the rule again. Needs the right to change the SQL server's firewall. Honours -WhatIf / -Confirm. Without it no firewall rule is changed.

parameters.name: EngineAppId
parameters.help: The engine application (client) id: receives the scoped send right only when no managed identity sends (a non-hosted engine); always checked for a tenant-wide Mail.Send.

parameters.name: RemoveEngineSpnAssignment
parameters.help: Also remove the engine application's older scoped assignment (off by default: it is scoped to the same mailbox and widens nothing).

parameters.name: AdminAppId
parameters.help: The Invardia Support app's client id, with -AdminSecret (unattended support / deploy). Leave it out to sign in in the browser as a person.

parameters.name: AdminSecret
parameters.help: The Invardia Support app's secret (the one allowed secret, framework 4.1a). Never printed. Never what a page or a document prints.

parameters.name: AdminCertThumbprint
parameters.help: Older callers only: a certificate of -AdminAppId instead of the secret. Not used by anything PIM Manager prints.

parameters.name: UseSignedInAccount
parameters.help: Use the signed-in az session (a person, or the Support app via Invardia's connect script) instead of the browser sign-in.

parameters.name: KeyVaultName
parameters.help: Older callers only: read the engine application id (secret Modern-AppId) from this vault when neither -EngineAppId nor a managed identity is given; needs -BootstrapAppId and -BootstrapThumbprint.

parameters.name: BootstrapAppId
parameters.help: Older callers only (see -KeyVaultName): the application that reads that vault.

parameters.name: BootstrapThumbprint
parameters.help: Older callers only (see -KeyVaultName): its certificate in the local machine store.

parameters.name: OutFile
parameters.help: Write the result as JSON here (for a deploy step). Under -WhatIf it is written only to a path in the temp folder.

parameters.name: TimeoutSeconds
parameters.help: How long to wait for Exchange administration to become usable.

parameters.name: ExchangeAdminDuration
parameters.help: Support app sign-in only: how long the time-bound Exchange Administrator role stays active (ISO 8601, PT15M..PT24H).

parameters.name: ExchangeReadyMinutes
parameters.help: How long to wait for a just-created Exchange organization that still refuses role assignments (1-240).

parameters.name: ExchangeReadyIntervalSeconds
parameters.help: How often to try again while waiting (10-900).

parameters.name: OnProgress
parameters.help: For a calling deploy: a script block that receives one plain progress line per wait.

readsOnly: Microsoft Graph: subscribedSkus (is there an Exchange Online plan beyond EXCHANGE_S_FOUNDATION), organization (the initial domain), the sending identities' and the engine's service principals and their app role assignments, the Microsoft Graph and Office 365 Exchange Online service principals (app role ids), users (the mailbox's UPN)
Microsoft Graph (Support app sign-in only): the setup app's app role assignments and its active directory roles (roleAssignmentScheduleInstances, roleDefinitions)
Exchange Online: Get-OrganizationConfig, Get-Mailbox, Get-ServicePrincipal, Get-ManagementScope, Get-ManagementRoleAssignment
Azure Resource Manager (only with -TickJobName / -ManagerAppName): the Container Apps job / container app (its managed identity)
PIM store (only with -SqlServerFqdn): pim.Settings, to read back what was stored
network: login.microsoftonline.com (sign-in; the browser answers on a localhost port)
whatIf: Signs in and reads everything above, then prints every change it would make: the mailbox to create, each Exchange registration, the scope and each scoped Application Mail.Send assignment, each tenant-wide Mail.Send it would remove, organization customization when needed, and the MailSender / MailMode it would store -- and makes none of them (no Exchange create or remove, no Graph write, no SQL connection). With the Support app sign-in, the app's own grants (Exchange.ManageAsApp, the time-bound Exchange Administrator) are previewed too; Exchange may then not be usable for the preview yet, which the run says ('steps [1]-[3] cannot be previewed; run without -WhatIf to apply').
undo: In Exchange Online: Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment for each *-MailSend assignment the run reported, Remove-ManagementScope <the scope it reported> (default <MailboxName>-SendScope; PIM4EntraPS-Sender on an install from before 2.4.538), Remove-ServicePrincipal for each registered identity, then remove the shared mailbox. In PIM Manager: Settings > Mail & alerting (another sender or mode). With the Support app sign-in also remove Exchange.ManageAsApp and RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory from the setup app if no longer wanted (the Exchange Administrator role expires by itself). A removed tenant-wide Mail.Send is not restored on purpose.
